Authors can now edit their own comments, but I haven't run or tested any of it, as you asked.

- **API:** `api/update-comment.ts` sends `PATCH /comments/{commentId}` with `{ body }`, checked by a Zod schema. On success it refetches the discussion's comments, using the key from `getInfiniteCommentsQueryOptions(discussionId).queryKey`. It also shows a "Comment Updated" success notification from inside the hook, per the project rule.
- **UI:** `components/update-comment.tsx` is an "Edit Comment" button that opens a form drawer pre-filled with the current body. It doesn't call `useNotifications` itself.
- **Comments list:** `comments-list.tsx` shows the Edit button next to Delete.
- **Visibility:** I added a `comment:update` policy in `lib/authorization.tsx` that is true only when the current user is the comment's author. Admins don't see Edit on other people's comments, even though they can delete them.
- **Mock backend:** I added a `PATCH` handler in `testing/mocks/handlers/comments.ts` that only updates comments owned by the requester. Without it the Edit button would fail against the mock API.

The `notes/` folder doesn't exist in this project, so I didn't create or update any notes.
